title: Generation of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ by extensions by zero of lisse sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $\mathcal G$ be the class of
objects $a_!L[n]$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ a locally
closed immersion, $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Every
$K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is obtained from objects of $\mathcal G$ by finitely many cones: there is
a finite sequence $K_1,\dots,K_N=K$ such that each $K_r$ is in $\mathcal G$ or is isomorphic to
the cone of a morphism between earlier members (up to shift). Conversely every such object
lies in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Define the finite construction witness with its stated generator predicate and shifted distinguished-cone relation. Prove that valid finite lists concatenate, and append one new cone after the two lists. Strong induction over the position in a witness proves its elimination principle. Applying this principle with the predicate of admitting a second kind of witness proves substitution of witnesses for all generators. These are explicit Fin.append and Fin.snoc constructions in Lean.

For the forward direction apply the generic bounded-cohomology finite cone witness to K. Each leaf is a shift of a constructible cohomology sheaf. Replace each leaf by its sheaf-filtration cone witness. The substitution lemma concatenates the finite data and preserves the last vertex K.

For the converse, the lisse-extension lemma puts each unshifted generator in the bounded constructible category. Specialize the existing triangulated theorem to the coefficient ring: split the coefficient disjunction and package the finite subextension as FiniteIntermediateField. Its repleteness and shift closure handle each shifted generator. Strong induction over the given finite witness uses cone closure and then undoes the output shift to establish membership of every entry and finally K.
